question: Does on-policy RL improve finite-budget target-directed molecular generation, and what is the effect of a fixed-prior KL regularizer?

tasks.disclosure: Fexofenadine was explored earlier using a different GRU; no fresh-blind claim

optimization.algorithm: on-policy REINFORCE with optional sequence KL in detached return
optimization.baseline: leave-one-out regularized returns for N>1; previous-batch EMA if N=1
optimization.ema_update_timing: after current update, detached current regularized-return batch mean
optimization.kl_aggregation: sum across actual trajectory actions including sampled SEP

budget.tail_batch: min(32, B - past_unique), chosen before sampling; keep every raw trajectory
budget.final_policy_budget: additional, uniform, never used for training or selection
budget.physical_compute_cache_accounting: per-run first identity counts logically even if global physical cache reused

evaluation.primary: normalized Top10 MPO AUC vs unique valid new evaluations
evaluation.early_stop_auc: last observed value carried forward with explicit actual unique count and stop reason; also report observed curve
evaluation.statistics: all seeds, mean/SD and paired differences; descriptive two-task result

engineering_checks_passed: pinned weight hash and missing-key-free load
cached rollout vs teacher-forcing logprob agreement
exact finite-MDP gradient and LOO baseline check
